claims.text: Resistance to simultaneous wear and corrosion in HEAs is governed primarily by the formation, stability, and mechanical integrity of a passivating surface oxide layer.
Multi-elemental composition enhances passivating oxide layers through sluggish diffusion and complex oxide chemistry.
The HEA begins with an equiatomic or near-equiatomic multi-principal-element composition.
The HEA begins with a homogeneous microstructure and no prior surface treatment.
A surface oxide layer forms during simultaneous mechanical wear and corrosive exposure.
The multi-elemental nature of HEAs promotes complex oxide formation.
The multi-elemental nature of HEAs promotes adherent and chemically stable oxide layers.
HEA oxide layers exhibit sluggish diffusion kinetics.
The proposed oxide layers resist mechanical removal during wear.
The proposed oxide layers resist chemical dissolution during corrosion.
The oxide-related synergistic effect reduces combined degradation relative to simpler-composition alloys.
HEAs will have lower combined material-loss rates than hardness- and microstructure-matched single- or binary-element baseline alloys.
The wear component of degradation will be lower in the HEA than in the baseline.
The corrosion component of degradation will be lower in the HEA than in the baseline.
When the oxide remains intact and stable, the HEA may show more than a 30% reduction in material loss.
The prediction applies when a stable surface oxide can form under the test environment.
The prediction may fail for HEAs lacking passivating elements.
The prediction may fail under extreme conditions that prevent oxide formation or rapidly remove the oxide.
